Captures were taken with --settle-ms 1400 because the focus tween runs 0.9 s; at the script's 300 ms default every named view is captured mid-tween, which is why the earlier mill frame read as a wide island shot.

Draw calls per composited frame (shadow + colour + post): overview 1800 -> 2902, fox 1255 -> 2029. The mill view was re-aimed at the wheel this revision (2.9,1.1,-1.9 d4.7 -> 3.5,1.25,-1.85 d6.4), so its 1060 -> 2075 is not like-for-like.

Scene objects: 1368 meshes + 94 InstancedMesh over 1859 instances (was 907 meshes + 5 InstancedMesh over 410); 314 distinct materials, 97 of them asked for through scene-kit.js and the rest by kit modules from the same kit-core cache.
Triangles in the composited overview frame: 335,679 (was 302,055 measured on the same view mid-rebuild; no pre-rebuild triangle reading exists for this view).
200-sample groundHeight/supportAt parity harness over the island: 0/200 differences before vs after the landscape rebuild.
World collider count 210 -> 164; the mill's declared solid is 11% smaller in volume than the box its meshes occupy, because the launder and hoist beam carry no collider.

The watermill blueprint's animate(dt) is never called: the hub at its `wheel` socket is re-hung under this scene's pivot and driven by the flow control. A test asserts the hub does not turn while the flow is closed.
limits: Software renderer only; no GPU, mobile or frame-rate certification.
Draw-call counts are a single reading per view, not a benchmark.
Draw calls rose 61% on the overview: blueprint detail is paid for in meshes. No attempt was made to hide it by dropping blueprint parts.
The three-tail fox, dragon and owl keep their authored meshes; only the moon deer moved to quadruped-walker. The blueprint always builds horns, hooves and one tail.

The moon deer is 1.2 m tall as before, but its rig is 1.7x the blueprint's default so the locked-stride envelope still fits the village's navigation gaps; at the blueprint's own proportions the deer could not route out of the pond meadow.
planVillage() is unused: a seeded plan would move every landmark the tests, focus presets and captures name.
Landmark solids are one AABB per building by contract (village-buildings.test.js asserts five), so a canopy or a launder that is high in the air still widens the box it is unioned into.

limits: One reading per view on one machine (Apple M4 Max, 40 GPU cores). Not a benchmark.

Under 2,000 draw calls at the overview was not reached: only the watermill has a bake, and a T0 blockout at the home view would be 90 px tall, so the proxy switch is clamped past the 40 m orbit ceiling.

No T1 level sits between T2 and T0 in the shipped LODs: at 40 m the inn's 1.2 m plaster tile is still 30 px, so a flat copy would cost a build and a pop and save no draw call. T1 remains the tier a host with no 2D canvas builds.
The T3 bake is frozen: no animate(dt), a wheel that cannot turn, and occlusion baked for one wheel orientation. That is why it is not the nearest LOD level.
The watermill kit is displayed at 0.42 scale, so its T2 tiles read about 2.4x finer than the pitch the proof captured; buildings/watermill.js exposes no size parameters.
captures/mill.png (537 kB) and captures/fox.png (520 kB) are over the 400 kB line the previous revision kept; re-encoding would invalidate the capture-log digests.
